messages.subject: stat_contour breaks and value missing
parts:
Hi all,

I'm using ggplot2 for some time but it is the first time I'm stick to
a problem.
When I use breaks to delimit contour in my plot with stat_contour, he
gives me this error "Error in if (empty(new)) return(data.frame()) :
value missing where TRUE / FALSE is required" (Literal translation
from french.)


i <- 0
out <- matrix(NA,1,4)
for (x in seq(1,20,by=1)){
for (y in seq(1,20,by=1)){
for (t in seq(1,9,by=1)){
z <- x*y*t
i <- i+1
out <- rbind(out,cbind(x,y,z,t))
}
}
}

ABC=data.frame(out[2:dim(out)[1],])
ABC.g <- (ggplot(ABC)
+ facet_wrap(~t)
+ geom_tile(aes(x=x,y=y,fill=z))
+
scale_fill_gradient2("z",low="red",high="blue",midpoint=551)
)
#The following example works fine
ABC.g+ stat_contour(aes(x=x,y=y,z=z))

#This one doesn't work at all
x11()
ABC.g + stat_contour(aes(x=x,y=y,z=z),breaks=c(500,1000))

My though is that the break value is out of the bounds in some of the
facets. My problem is very similar to this one :
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/1392f58e6aca7739/539650414d31736f?lnk=gst&q=facet+stat_contour#539650414d31736f

If there are any ways to get rid of the error ?

I'm using the last version of ggplot2 (0.8.9)


Thanks you !
RL.

An upper limit of 400 would be consistent with the idea that a break has
to appear in every facet:

> ddply(ABC, .(t), summarise, range=t(range(z)))
t range.1 range.2
1 1 1 400
2 2 2 800
3 3 3 1200
4 4 4 1600
5 5 5 2000
6 6 6 2400
7 7 7 2800
8 8 8 3200
9 9 9 3600

> ABC.g + stat_contour(aes(x=x,y=y,z=z),breaks=c(8, 500, 1000))

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: stat_contour breaks and value missing
parts:
Hi,

I am not sure that this is something to "fix" per se beyond as others
have mentioned making sure at least one break is within range for all
facets.

If anyone is interested in working on this, below is a minimal
example. It seems to me the "problem" comes up on lines 18-27 of
stat-contour.r because an oddly formed list ends up getting passed
rather than an empty data frame.

###############
dat <- data.frame(x = rep(1:4, 4), y = rep(1:4, each = 4),
z = 1:16, g = factor(rep(1:2, each = 8)))

## works
ggplot(dat) +
stat_contour(aes(x = x, y = y, z = z), breaks = 12)

## fails because all breaks are out of range for one facet
ggplot(dat) +
facet_wrap(~g) +
stat_contour(aes(x = x, y = y, z = z), breaks = 12)
###############


In the meantime, Romain, if you just want nothing to be plotted in
facets where the breaks are out of range, this seems to work for me at
least in the few cases I tested. Load ggplot2, then copy and paste
the code below which will create a version of stat_contour in your
workspace so it will be used over the one from ggplot2. I added a
small section that if all breaks are outside the range, it will issue
a warning and return an empty data frame, which should have the side
effect of nothing being plotted in that facet. I attached the results
I get from your example after using my modifaction.

Hope this helps,

Josh


StatContour <- proto(Stat, {
calculate <- function(., data, scales, bins=NULL, binwidth=NULL,
breaks = NULL, na.rm = FALSE, ...) {
data <- remove_missing(data, na.rm, name = "stat_contour")

# If no parameters set, use pretty bins
if (is.null(bins) && is.null(binwidth) && is.null(breaks)) {
breaks <- pretty(range(data$z), 10)
}
# If provided, use bins to calculate binwidth
if (!is.null(bins)) {
binwidth <- diff(range(data$z)) / bins
}
# If necessary, compute breaks from binwidth
if (is.null(breaks)) {
breaks <- fullseq(range(data$z), binwidth)
}
# section added to avoid errors when breaks are out of range
if (all(breaks < min(data$z) | breaks > max(data$z))) {
warning("All specified breaks are outside the range of z
no contours will be drawn in this plot/facet")
contour_df <- data.frame(level = NULL, x = NULL, y= NULL,
piece = NULL, group = NULL)
return(contour_df)
}

z <- tapply(data$z, data[c("x", "y")], identity)
cl <- contourLines(
x = sort(unique(data$x)), y = sort(unique(data$y)), z = z,
levels = breaks)
cl <- lapply(cl, as.data.frame)

contour_df <- rbind.fill(cl)
contour_df$piece <- rep(seq_along(cl), sapply(cl, nrow))
contour_df$group <- paste(data$group[1], contour_df$piece, sep = "-")
contour_df
}

objname <- "contour"
desc <- "Contours of 3d data"

icon <- function(.) GeomContour$icon()

default_geom <- function(.) GeomPath
default_aes <- function(.) aes(order = ..level..)
required_aes <- c("x", "y", "z")
desc_outputs <- list(
level = "z value of contour"
)
})

     warning("All specified breaks are outside the range of z
     no contours will be drawn in this plot/facet")
     contour_df <- data.frame(level = NULL, x = NULL, y= NULL,
       piece = NULL, group = NULL)
     return(contour_df)
   }

   z <- tapply(data$z, data[c("x", "y")], identity)
   cl <- contourLines(
     x = sort(unique(data$x)), y = sort(unique(data$y)), z = z,
     levels = breaks)
   cl <- lapply(cl, as.data.frame)

   contour_df <- rbind.fill(cl)
   contour_df$piece <- rep(seq_along(cl), sapply(cl, nrow))
   contour_df$group <- paste(data$group[1], contour_df$piece, sep = "-")
   contour_df
 }

 objname <- "contour"
 desc <- "Contours of 3d data"

 icon <- function(.) GeomContour$icon()

 default_geom <- function(.) GeomPath
 default_aes <- function(.) aes(order = ..level..)
 required_aes <- c("x", "y", "z")
 desc_outputs <- list(
   level = "z value of contour"
 )
})
